w: Swamishri arrived at Center Parcs at 7.50 pm for the 4-day Kishore - Kishori Shibir. The much awaited exciting and enlightening shibir was attended by 260 kishores and 220 kishoris.

In the opening session Swamishri said, "Kishore Mandal's Jay. I am very happy to see your love and enthusiasm. The venue of the shibir is very nice. You have to pass through a maze of buildings to get here. And you can get lost in the maze. You are all lost in the maze (of life) so you have to come out! We have come here to get you out. Do you understand?... Only one who knows the way can get you out of the maze. God and the holy Sadhu are our friends, relatives and well-wishers..." The 4-day shibir program from 27 to 30 June included videos, slide shows, narrations by kishores on 'Swami cares', explanations about murtis and holy relics in Swamishri's puja, 'Ruchi' quiz, question - answer session and sports.

Saanskrutik Virasat The evening Children’s Day special program was held at the Anaheim Convention Center. The LA Children’s forum presented ‘Sanskrutik Virasat’ which depicted the stories of Shravan, Dhruv and Nachiketa. Thereafter dignitaries honored Swamishri. Finally Swamishri said in his blessings, “Today nobody has any time, but they have time to go to parties. But one’s home is like a big party. Whatever wealth and name you may have achieved will be of no good if your children become corrupt, sinful and terrorists. So there is a need to be vigilant while raising children. You are vigilant in your business. So, too, you must be awakened in matters about raising your children. You should also listen to them with love and care…” The devotees and well-wishers appreciated the evening program.

Thursday

At 8.25 pm the evening satsang assembly had concluded in the mandir. Swamishri was walking back to his room. On either side of his pathway devotees were standing for Swamishri’s darshan. On seeing a devotee Swamishri asked, “Piyush, are you well?” “Yes,” he replied. “Do you come to the mandir?” “Swami, I live 100 miles away.” “Let it be 100 miles away, but you can come to the mandir two to four times a month,” Swamishri emphasised. On seeing Swamishri’s insistence, Piyush tried to shunt the track of conversation, “Swami, I have pledged for some donations to the Atladra mandir. That donation…” Swamishri interrupted midway and said, “Listen to what I have to say! Do come to the mandir. And if the mandir is too far then you have a little mandir in your house. Come to this mandir once a month, but do the arti, puja, thal and home discourse at your home mandir every day. And be careful not to eat meat and fall into bad company. You must assemble all the family members and read satsang books, sing dhun and kirtans. By so doing your house will become a mandir.” For spiritual progress it is essential to engage ourselves in some spiritual endeavours on a daily basis. Otherwise, the material influences of society and our own base instincts dilute or annul our devotional feelings, faith and morals. Hence, Swamishri prescribes regular attendance to mandir, daily performance of devotional rituals and reading of scriptures.

Whenever his little grandson cried a local man of Bhadra would place a bidi in his mouth. Subsequently, the little child became addicted. Presently, he is three and a half years old and eats two packets of gutkha (tobacco) daily. When he does not get the gutkha he throws a tantrum. The boy's father and grandfather are addicted to gutkha and bidi.

Sometimes, the child goes all by himself to the local shop to get a gutkha under his father's name. The innocent, tender child has become habituated to tobacco all because of his father and grandfather's mistake.

The child's uncle, who is a devotee and lives in Surat, brought him for Swamishri’s darshan. He placed him on the rostrum. Swamishri welcomed him, “Jai Swaminarayan.” But the ignorant little child did not know what to say. He simply looked down and remained quiet. Swamishri asked for a box of prasad, and taking a sweet ball from it, said, “Take this, and don't eat gutkha. Gutkha spoils your body and causes disease. Therefore don't eat it.”
Swamishri's compassion for the little, tender child was apparent to all. To release him from the shackles of addiction Swamishri blessed him and advised him and his relatives.

During lunch, Harshadbhai Rana (Nairobi), seated in front, said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "When we come into your presence, your image settles in us, but then it disappears again and other images come. What is the reason for that?"
"Ask within yourself what the reason is."
"Only if you bless us with your glance can we understand the reason," said Pandya.
Reinforcing Swamishri's words, Harshadbhai Rana said, "Give us such strength that we always keep looking within."
"I have already given strength. That is why you are able to come here from Nairobi. Otherwise, who would leave earning money and come here?"
"This strength remains only as long as you bless us with your glance."

"My glance is always there. It is only because Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj are seated here that you are able to come. Otherwise no one could leave the attachment to money and come." Swamishri took note of how devotees leave their thriving businesses to come and benefit, and at the same time gave the understanding that each must look within himself.

After his meal, having met about 100 devotees, Pramukh Swami Maharaj, who sees all equally, met Bharat, a man with a learning disability who has been doing seva here for years. As if born only to repay a debt to the mandir from a previous life, Bharat does seva with such devotion, locking his mind into the work of the mandir. Swamishri lovingly spent ten minutes with him. He said to Bharat, "Bharat! What work do you do?"

Bharat said, "In the morning I put ghee on the rotlis for the devotees. I serve food to the devotees. I wash the devotees' dishes. I clean the mandir." He presented a long list. Then someone said, "He does all this seva, but sometimes he also swears."
Swamishri immediately said to Bharat, "Stop swearing. Devotees should not come and tell us, 'Do you keep such a person in the mandir?' So that no one says that, from now on do not swear."
Then someone asked, "Bharat! Do you want to get married?"
"I definitely do not want to get married."
"Why?" Swamishri asked.

"You would have to regret it." At Bharat's answer Swamishri burst out laughing and said, "Even he understands this." Taking the conversation further, Swamishri asked, "So many devotees get married. Do they all regret it?"
With this argument of Swamishri's, what was in Bharat's heart came out.
Bharat said, "What you say is true, but one would have to look for someone one likes!"
Hearing this, Swamishri again laughed loudly and, helping him see the world as it is, said, "Bharat! We do not have to look for anything. Doing seva here is just right."

Every year the city of Amdavad celebrates the popular festival of Rath Yatra with pomp and joy. The murtis of Bhagwan Shri Jagannath, Balaram and Subhadra are ceremoniously carried in floats from the Jagannath Mandir through the streets of Amdavad all day.

The Rath Yatra festival was also celebrated by Swamishri at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Amdavad. Swamishri arrived for Thakorji’s darshan at 7.20 am. A golf cart was transformed into a decorated rath. Swamishri performed pujan of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Bhagwan Jagannath. Thereafter Swamishri sat in the rath and performed five pradakshinas of the mandir. In the lead were dancing children dressed in traditional clothes. Then sadhus followed, singing bhajans and charging the air with devotion and festivity. Behind Swamishri’s rath were many leading devotees. And all around the festive path thousands of devotees were singing and joyfully absorbing the festive darshan. In conclusion, Swamishri’s chariot was steered into the main auditorium. The singing and dancing by children and youths made the occasion devotional and divine. Swamishri was seated with folded hands, blessing the devotees as the rath proceeded towards the stage.

During Swamishri’s puja sadhus sang bhajans on the rath yatra festival. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and arti of Maharaj’s murti. In the evening assembly Swamishri steered Shri Harikrishna Maharaj on a small rath with a remote control console. Thereafter in his blessings he said, “Man loves festivals. Shriji Maharaj celebrated festivals. Though he was God, he celebrated Janmashtmi, Ram Navmi, Rath Yatra and other festivals. He added the elements of spiritual discourses and bhajans so that one could strike a rapport with God. Maharaj reformed the prevailing gatherings into festivals of devotion, worship and wisdom.”

During Pramukh Swami Maharaj's walk, the "Yagnapurush Charitam" was being read. In it came the incident of Shastriji Maharaj sitting in a tub to cross the river at Radhu. So Yogicharan Swami asked Swamishri, "Did Shastriji Maharaj know how to swim?"
"No. Neither he nor Yogiji Maharaj." Saying this, he said emphatically, "They may not have known how to swim, but both he and Yogiji Maharaj have carried us across."

ds.t: "If there is no unity, there is nothing"
w: A leader of the youth wing of a political party came for darshan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj said to him, "Keep unity and oneness. If there is no unity, there is nothing. Forget everything and live in unity."

A leader of the youth wing of a political party came for darshan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj said to him, "Keep unity and oneness. If there is no unity, there is nothing. Forget everything and live together in unity."

Mahant Swami Maharaj performed arti in the mandir at 5.45. Here various pictures had been placed to be sanctified by Swamishri's glance. Among them was a picture of Shriji Maharaj standing with his mare Manki. Seeing the expression on Shriji Maharaj's face, Swamishri said, "He is in a powerful mood...!" Everyone laughed. Swamishri's power of reading art and feelings is wonderful.
Dr Asif Taufiq came to meet Mahant Swami Maharaj. Swamishri was very pleased to meet him and himself embraced him. The doctor was overwhelmed.
He said, "I met Mahant Swamiji two years ago, but today the energy seemed somewhat different. I experienced radiance upon radiance. And I am a Muslim, yet he embraced me!"
Atmaswarupdas Swami said, "He does not look at you as a Muslim at all."
Asifji said, "Yes, he looks at people as human beings."
Kneeling close to Swamishri, he said, "I am a Muslim, yet I find joy in meeting you. You just eat, maintain the weight and take proper rest."

Today, as every day, during the walk there was the benefit of a reading from Yogi Vani and Mahant Swami Maharaj's commentary. In it was read: "If we go about carrying attachment, there can be no true association. All of it must be given up."

Swamishri said, "To have it and give it up is hard. If one does not have it, it is already given up. Raghuvirji Maharaj, it is amazing, but what status he had! What power he must have had! Yet he came as a pilgrim! But the best use of power is its nonuse."
Viveknidhidas Swami said, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj too never used power on anyone, and you do not use it either."
Swamishri said, "If one sees the other person as separate, power gets used."
The great sadhu considers all of us his own.
In every action of Swamishri, some thought is always woven in.

ds.t: Forgiven for those who are open
w: As Mahant Swami Maharaj was leaving the assembly, Vivekmurtidas Swami had it asked: "Ask Swamishri whether only the faults of those who were in the assembly are forgiven, or also of all those who were watching the webcast?"

Walking along, Swamishri said, "No, of those who became open (without deceit)." (At the start of the assembly, the teenage boys and girls had opened their hearts to Swamishri through letters. At that time Swamishri himself had asked for the microphone and said, "May Maharaj and Swami forgive everyone's faults.") Through one short sentence, Swamishri made it clear that only one who behaves without deceit becomes worthy of the great sadhu's grace.

After the chesta was over, Gnanpriyadas Swami asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "In assemblies and meetings, sometimes your wishes are not respected and things happen that you do not like, yet you immediately adjust and accept it gladly. With what thought do you do this?"
Swamishri said, "To give everyone the benefit, to please everyone."
Truly, who is supposed to please whom? The disciples the guru, or the guru the disciples?
